answers.core: Actually, it being an addon might be a good compromise that could get the feature added for those who want it, while still allowing anybody who thinks it unsafe to use getters and setters as usual.  But add-ons aren't typically used to change core features of the language.  I think there will be ideological arguments against making an add-on just to expose members.

While it is only 3 lines of code with the old method, it is 149 characters with the old method, versus a mere 24 characters in the method I proposed.  Given that transforms and velocities will be accessed hundreds of times in the code, it adds up to a significant nuisance for programmers to deal with.  It took over a minute just to add 1 to a variable, it's unacceptable for rapid prototyping.
Enough so that I figure there must be a pretty big reason for Godot to work the way that it does.  However, I haven't found anything substantial yet.  I don't see how making the actual transform a protected member would be unsafe code, as it would still be protected.
